name: TESSERA Corponation Executive Aegis Wand EAW-1 'Silhouette'
description:
The EAW-1 'Silhouette' is TESSERA's entry into the executive personal defense market — a device so carefully designed to avoid looking like a weapon that it has become the definitive example of what the category can achieve. The Silhouette is a 38-centimeter carbon-fiber rod, 12mm in diameter, with a matte black finish and a single brushed-steel accent ring near the base. In its carrying configuration, it nestles inside a custom-fitted sleeve built into the lining of a compatible TESSERA Executive Series briefcase, or alternatively within the hollow shaft of a TESSERA-branded umbrella accessory sold separately. In either configuration, it passes visual inspection, standard metal detection (the carbon-fiber construction contains no ferrous metal), and even casual physical search by someone who does not know to look for it.

The Silhouette's discharge system is among the most refined available in any sub-military shock device. TESSERA's engineering team spent three development cycles optimizing the contact electrode array — a 4-centimeter active zone at the rod's tip — to deliver a precisely shaped 180,000-volt pulse with a waveform specifically tuned to maximize disruption across the augmentation profiles most common in Tier 4-5 business environments: light BCI systems, cosmetic subdermal implants, and standard executive health-monitoring chrome. A secondary pulse mode, accessible through a second grip press, activates a partial EMP burst that disrupts non-hardened electronics within the 4-centimeter contact zone — sufficient to crash a standard BCI or disable a smartwatch, but calibrated below the full anti-cyberware damage threshold of TESSERA's NSR-1 line.

At Φ8,500, the Silhouette is priced as a luxury item and positioned as one. TESSERA's marketing materials feature it alongside premium accessories and describe it as 'the standard of discreet personal confidence.' It is sold through TESSERA's authorized executive retail network, requiring a standard stun device license and a TESSERA Executive Client registration that, in practice, functions as a social vetting process — TESSERA does not sell the Silhouette to people they deem inconsistent with the brand.
legality: Licensed — stun device classification; carbon-fiber construction passes standard metal detection; concealment in briefcase/umbrella accessory legal under personal carry provisions; sale restricted to TESSERA Executive Client registrants

tactical_use: The Silhouette is a surprise weapon — its entire design philosophy is premised on the target not knowing it is there until the moment of deployment. The 38-centimeter length is precisely calibrated for deployment from a briefcase grip (drawing and striking in a single motion) or from an umbrella handle (grip reversal and contact). TESSERA's recommended use case is defense against close-quarters threats in professional environments: the lobby altercation, the elevator confrontation, the parking structure approach. The secondary EMP mode is recommended for use against BCI-equipped aggressors as a disorienting first strike before physical contact.
cultural_context: Among Tier 4-5 professionals who know about it, the Silhouette carries a specific kind of social cachet — it is the weapon of someone who has thought carefully about personal security and has the resources and taste to address it elegantly. Owning one is rarely disclosed; it tends to be discovered in retrospect, when someone has used one, or when a peer mentions it in the context of personal security recommendations. In Tier 5 social circles, asking 'are you carrying an Aegis?' is a coded way of asking whether someone takes their personal security seriously. The phrase 'wand work' has entered discreet professional slang for any situation where an executive has defended themselves — a deliberate aestheticization of violence that smooths over its reality.
known_users: high-end private investigators on retainer to corporate clients
story_hooks: A Silhouette registered to a senior TESSERA executive is recovered from the scene of an apparent mugging in a Tier 3 transit hub — but the executive reported the briefcase stolen two weeks earlier and has an alibi. The discharge log shows the weapon was fired once, three days ago, in a location that corresponds to an unoccupied TESSERA research annex. The 'mugging victim' in the transit hub — whose BCI was partially fried by what appears to be the Silhouette's EMP mode — was a TESSERA internal auditor who was three days from finalizing a report.

physical_description.visual_profile: A deceptively elegant black rod, barely thicker than a pen, with the presence of high-end industrial design rather than a weapon. Its refined proportions suggest a luxury writing instrument or precision tool — something you'd expect to see clipped to an executive's desk, not wielded in combat.
physical_description.dimensions: 38 cm length, 12 mm diameter. The active electrode array occupies the final 4 cm of the tip.
physical_description.weight_description: Featherlight in hand — 0.19 kg — with a balance point near the grip that makes it feel almost weightless during deployment. Deceptive: the carbon-fiber construction provides rigidity without heft.
physical_description.primary_material: Carbon-fiber composite (non-ferrous), engineered to defeat ferrous metal detection entirely.
physical_description.finish: Matte black throughout, with a single brushed-steel accent ring positioned 6 cm from the base. The accent ring catches light subtly, suggesting careful manufacturing rather than aggressive aesthetics.
physical_description.color_scheme: Matte charcoal black with brushed steel ring. The electrode tip is a faint silver-grey where the carbon-fiber gives way to the contact array.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured polymer grip section (approximately 10 cm from base), designed for secure but comfortable palming. The grip material has a subtle diamond-knurl pattern — expensive, tactile, professional.
distinctive_features: Electrode array at tip appears as a faint segmented ring, almost invisible unless examined closely
Single brushed-steel accent ring serves both aesthetic and functional purpose (charging contact interface)
No visible seams, vents, or indicator lights — design aggressively minimalist
Tapered slightly toward the tip, creating impression of a writing instrument
Carbon-fiber weave visible under matte coating as fine lines running length of shaft
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Small TESSERA logo (Φ symbol integrated into design) laser-etched on the grip section, barely visible without direct light. Serial number etched on the opposite side, equally discreet. No model designation visible on the device itself.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine to lightly used. TESSERA clientele maintain these with the care afforded to luxury accessories — microfiber cloth included with purchase. Battle-worn examples are rare; the Silhouette is a surprise weapon, not a workhorse.
